title: Gain on a sale: amount realized and adjusted basis
rule: Gain on a sale is the amount realized less adjusted basis; a loss is the reverse. The amount realized is money plus the fair market value of property received, and generally includes liabilities the sale discharges, such as a mortgage the buyer assumes or a nonrecourse loan the property is sold subject to. Costs paid to facilitate the sale, such as commissions, reduce the amount realized and are not deducted or added to basis; a dealer in property deducts them. Adjusted basis is the basis, generally cost, raised by capital expenditures and lowered by depreciation: the amount allowable, claimed or not, or a larger amount allowed that reduced tax.
changeWatch: Amendments to sections 1001, 1011, 1012 or 1016(a)(1) and (2), or to the rule on amounts paid to sell property in 26 CFR 1.263(a)-1(e) or the rule on liabilities discharged by a sale in 26 CFR 1.1001-2(a); the IRS reissues Publication 544 each year (the 2025 edition was current on 2026-11-14).
